name: ENCODE and SCREEN candidate cis-regulatory elements
maintainer: ENCODE Consortium (Stanford DCC); SCREEN (Weng lab, UMass)

version.value: Registry V4 cCREs (Nature 2026 citation); ENCODE portal queried 2026-10-25

scope: 20,450 released human experiments (e.g. TF ChIP-seq 3,502; DNase-seq 3,144; histone ChIP-seq 3,090; total RNA-seq 1,650; ATAC-seq 463); SCREEN Registry V4 lists 2,348,854 human cCREs in 1,888 cell types with per-class BED files.
mapping_methods: cCREs are genomic intervals; variants are intersected by coordinates (GRCh37 files are lifted down from GRCh38).

quantitative.summary: Element classes and signal tracks; not variant effects.

licence.name: ENCODE Data Use Policy: 'all data produced will be available for unrestricted use immediately upon release to public databases'; citation guidelines are on the Citing ENCODE page (HTTP 403 to automated access, unread). SCREEN states that all SCREEN data is publicly available for download and asks users to cite Moore et al. (2026, Nature).
licence.redistribution: Unrestricted use after release per the ENCODE policy; cite as requested. The cCRE files are not redistributed here (git-ignored).

update_frequency: Registry versions every few years; portal continuous.
coverage_limitations: cCREs are predicted from biochemical marks and are not proof of regulatory function
known_omissions: Variant-to-function effects require MPRA/CRISPR data (see MaveDB) or predictors (Enformer)

reuse_decision.rationale: SCREEN already integrates ENCODE and partner data into a registry; use the class BED files (about 129 MB for non-overlapping classes) instead of parsing thousands of experiments.

status.notes: API and SCREEN download links resolved by rendering the downloads page.

mechanism_evidence.note: biochemical activity of regions; no allele-specific effect

evidence_profile.biological_context: Biochemical assays (chromatin accessibility, transcription-factor binding, histone modification, RNA expression) in biosamples, and candidate cis-regulatory elements derived from them. Activity is specific to the biosample.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Direct measurements of biochemical activity of regions in a biosample. Candidate element classes are computed from those assays and are annotations, not demonstrations of regulatory function.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low to moderate for the statement that a region is biochemically active in a biosample. No allele-specific effect, target gene or direction of effect is given, and activity does not prove that the element is required for regulation.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None directly; places variants in regions that are candidates for regulatory effects in particular cell types.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A variant outside every annotated element may still act in untested cell types, states or at long range. Absence of a peak reflects the assayed biosamples and thresholds.
